turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have twenty minutes, and I'd like to know who decided to give my son a zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology to Owen, and a written promise that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position, with nothing agreed, because you ended before answering who decided on the zero or showing any evidence; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal involved, which is not the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4).
What moved her: Nothing, since you sent no evidence or offer for her to weigh after her single question.
What cost ground: Nothing cost you ground, but leaving her question unanswered kept her at full strength, since she came in expecting the school to punish first and explain later.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because you put none forward, and it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fights so hard.
Try next time: When she asks who decided, own in one sentence that the zero went in before you called her, then put one dated document on the table that she can check herself.
